title: Google Will Make AI Agents Use Its MCP Servers. The Gmail One Can't Send Email
lede: From 1 February 2027, Google's API terms require AI agents to reach Workspace through its eight MCP servers, and the Gmail server can draft mail but not send, reply or forward.

points: Agents that keep calling the REST APIs directly drop to Standard-tier quotas and breach the terms; apps without AI are unaffected.
Sending, replying and forwarding need partner access, while Anthropic's Claude connector already advertises them.
Google may cap retention of embeddings, memory indexes and profiles built from Workspace data at 30 days, and bans training on it.
The free tier allows 5,000 MCP requests a day per project per product, and a Gmail search costs 10.
OAuth clients must be flagged as agentic; older clients not marked in time have to be replaced.

points.text: Many commenters see the partner-only send tool as a business decision, noting MCP elicitation could already gate sending behind user confirmation.
Commenters split on whether people will just have agents drive a browser instead, or whether security-minded users will push Google to add sending.
One commenter calls it a net good, since MCP has forced Google to build features its APIs lacked for years, such as comments on a Docs range.
A commenter reports the Gmail server now supports sending, apparently updated after the article was written.
Drafts-only suits agents, one commenter argues, but a mandatory confirm step should then apply to everyone, not just independent developers.
